dataset.name: Sundarbans, West Bengal (illustrative)
dataset.description: Illustrative coastal change: spatially varying erosion and accretion, mudflat belts and mangrove cover around tidal rivers and islands.
dataset.simulated_label: Illustrative Dataset: a generated demonstration layer, not satellite imagery.
dataset.source: Generated by the reusable pipeline app.explorer.atlas; no satellite data are used for these layers.

rules: Shorelines move with a smooth random field: some stretches erode, others accrete, and the exposed south erodes more often.
Mudflat is the intertidal band next to land; mangrove needs land above a minimum height, so new land becomes mangrove only after it has emerged.

trend.method: Theil-Sen slope with Kendall tau test on yearly same-season open water area

confidence_reasons: mean valid-pixel share of the observations used: 100%
0% of the footprint is uncertain (cloud or gaps) and excluded
each end rests on a single yearly observation
limitations: Illustrative Dataset: a generated demonstration layer, not satellite imagery. Results show the method working on known, built-in changes.
Spatial resolution is about 41 m per pixel; no positional-noise filter is applied to this classification product, so single-pixel changes are kept.
Only Jan were compared so that seasons match; other months were not used for the start/end maps.
The data describe where and how much open water extent changed. They cannot, by themselves, establish why.
what_was_analysed: Same-season composites of 2000 (1 observations) and 2020 (1 observations), using only Jan so seasons match. A pixel counts as open water if it is open water in at least 50% of its valid observations; 0 ha (0%) were uncertain and excluded.
